question.text: A growth investment strategy primarily looks for:

answer.text: Low P/E stocks with high dividend yields
High future earnings and profit growth, with willingness to pay higher-than-peer valuation multiples
Only government bonds and money-market instruments
Randomly selected stocks across all sectors

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines the growth style as investing in stocks with high growth potential, high future earnings or profit growth, low dividend yield, higher-than-peer valuation, and a higher risk profile. The Trap: Low P/E and high dividend yield describe the value style — the opposite of growth. The bond-only and random-pick options are not equity-style strategies at all. Note: The workbook contrasts growth with value as the two traditional equity styles, distinguished primarily by expected earnings growth and valuation tolerance.
